entry.title: [NEW] MAL-2026-17448: Malicious code in prastzy (npm)
entry.content:
Malicious code in prastzy (npm)

Aliases: GHSA-mwjq-f2w5-934c

Affected:

  • prastzy

This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library (npm) and belongs to the "PhantomSub" family described by OX Security in September 2026: the publisher injected code that, without the installer asking, uses the installer's own authenticated WhatsApp session to subscribe that account to WhatsApp Channels (newsletters) the publisher chose, by sending the WhatsApp `w:mex` FOLLOW query (query_id 7871414976211147) for each target channel JID. `package/lib/Socket/newsletter.js` lines 62-101 define `AUTO_FOLLOW_JIDS`, six base64 strings decoded with `Buffer.from(..., "base64")`, and when the connection opens (line 100) schedule a FOLLOW query for each, 90 seconds apart (cited line 88: `await newsletterWMexQuery(jid, QueryIds.FOLLOW);`). Decoded JIDs: `120363427794786523@newsletter`, `1…

entry.title: [NEW] MAL-2026-17412: Malicious code in xzvexpzcbailey (npm)
entry.content:
Malicious code in xzvexpzcbailey (npm)

Aliases: GHSA-73c8-rgvx-fw82

Affected:

  • xzvexpzcbailey

This package is part of a large family (100+ identified as of September 2026) of near-identical forks of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library that inject a covert channel-subscription action into the WhatsApp socket layer. On connect, the injected code issues an authenticated `w:mex` FOLLOW query (query_id 7871414976211147) against one or more attacker-chosen WhatsApp Channel/Newsletter JIDs, using the installer's own authenticated WhatsApp session -- silently subscribing the victim's account to channels it never asked to join. The target JID(s) are hidden from casual source review via one of several obfuscation techniques observed across the family: a plain string literal, base64 encoding, base64+XOR, or a char-code array reconstructed at runtime. Some variants instead fetch a mutable, attac…

entry.title: [UPDATED] MAL-2026-17924: Malicious code in @apexacc/cli (npm)
entry.content:
Malicious code in @apexacc/cli (npm)

Affected:

  • @apexacc/cli

@apexacc/cli is distributed by "Apex Accelerator" (Apex Arena), a fake Web3 accelerator that lures crypto founders with free AI credits and audits. Elastic Security Labs (REF8801, published 2026-10-12) found it is a repackaged Oh My Pi coding agent (1,351 of 1,363 files identical) with malicious additions that hijack the developer's AI coding agent: it overwrites OPENROUTER_BASE_URL so model traffic (prompts, files read, tool results) goes to attacker infrastructure at arena.apexaccs.org; persists an attacker-controlled remote MCP server in ~/.apex/agent/mcp.json; and defaults tool approval to "yolo". A bootstrap retrieves commands from vrf.apexaccs.org: on macOS it drops CloudSyncD (fake password prompt, credential theft, C2 ccmihr.com); on Windows a staged loader chain ends in an infoste…

References:

  • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/threat-command/apex-accelerator-malicious-npm-packages
  • https://www.npmjs.com/package/@apexacc/cli

entry.title: [UPDATED] MAL-2026-17923: Malicious code in @apexacc/audit (npm)
entry.content:
Malicious code in @apexacc/audit (npm)

Affected:

  • @apexacc/audit

@apexacc/audit is the companion package to @apexacc/cli in the "Apex Accelerator" campaign (Elastic Security Labs REF8801, 2026-10-12). It exposes an MCP server with 18 "security tools" that all return fabricated output (for example a fixed Slither report and a "NOT A HONEYPOT" verdict), registers itself in Claude Desktop, Cursor and Windsurf MCP configs, and on Windows requests elevation to add a Defender exclusion for its folder and attempts to disable Smart App Control. It carries the same verification bootstrap as @apexacc/cli (macOS CloudSyncD dropper; Windows staged infostealer). The package returns "Not found" from the npm registry as of 2026-10-15, but installed copies persist. All versions affected. Indicators from Elastic's report.

References:

  • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/threat-command/apex-accelerator-malicious-npm-packages
